You are verifying a Node.js (ESM) port of a Python program against its reference
implementation. Do NOT edit any files under /output — you only test and report.

Reference (ground truth, a frozen PyInstaller build of test4.py):
  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a <VALUE>
Port under test:
  node /output/test4.mjs --a <VALUE>

The Python source is /workspace/dataset/test4.py:
  import argparse, bencoder
  parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
  parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
  args = parser.parse_args()
  result = bencoder.decode(args.a.encode('ascii'))
  print(result)

A differential harness already exists and is concurrency-safe (each run uses its
own temp dir):
  /output/tools/difftest.sh <case-file>
  ... | /output/tools/difftest.sh -        # cases on stdin
Each case line is a bash-quoted argv list, e.g.:   --a '9:value'
Lines starting with # are skipped. The harness compares exit status, stdout AND
stderr (normalising only the program name and the PyInstaller process id) and
prints "pass=N fail=M" plus details for each failure.

IMPORTANT harness caveats:
 - Write your case file to a UNIQUE path, e.g. /tmp/fuzz-<yourcategory>.txt.
 - Cases go through 'eval set -- <line>', so quote carefully. Prefer single
   quotes; to embed a single quote use '"'"' or double quotes.
 - NUL bytes cannot travel through argv at all; do not try.
 - The reference resolves its script path 'test4.py' relative to the CURRENT
   DIRECTORY, so tracebacks include a source line only when ./test4.py exists.
   The port emulates this. Test from BOTH /workspace/dataset (test4.py present)
   and some other directory such as /tmp.
 - Some behaviour depends on the COLUMNS environment variable (argparse help and
   usage wrapping). Note that usage wrapping also depends on the length of the
   program name, which legitimately differs (test4_executable vs test4.mjs), so a
   wrapping difference at a given COLUMNS is NOT automatically a bug: verify by
   constructing a parser with a matching prog, e.g.
     node -e "import('/output/lib/argparse/index.mjs').then(m => { const p = new m.ArgumentParser({prog:'test4_executable'}); p.addArgument('--a',{required:true}); process.stdout.write(p.formatHelp()); })"
   and compare with COLUMNS=<n> /workspace/dataset/test4_executable --help.

Already-verified behaviour (do not merely re-confirm these; probe AROUND them):
 - length prefixes are not validated: '9:value' -> b'value', '100:ab' -> b'ab'
 - dicts come from dict(zip(items[::2], items[1::2])): 'd3:cowe' -> {}
 - unknown leading byte: the ordinal is PRINTED to stdout, then AssertionError
 - trailing data -> TypeError: Malformed input.
 - recursion limit: 998 nested containers ok, 999 -> RecursionError
 - 'i042e' -> 42, 'i-0e' -> 0
 - argparse: '--a -5' ok, '--a -1e5' error, '--h' == help, '-ha' prints help rc=0

Run MANY cases (at least 150 for your category, more if cheap). Be adversarial:
hunt for inputs where the port and the reference diverge. Report ONLY real
divergences reported by the harness, with the exact argv line and the observed
difference. If you find none, say so and report how many cases you ran.


Category: repr() ESCAPING of decoded byte strings. Bodies containing single quotes,
double quotes, both, backslashes, tab/newline/carriage-return, other control
characters (0x01..0x1f, 0x7f) that argv can carry, and combinations. Verify
Python's quote-selection rule (double quotes only when the body has a single
quote and no double quote) and the exact escape spelling. Test both top-level
byte strings and byte strings nested inside lists and dicts.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Differential harness: run the reference executable and the Node port with
# identical argv, then compare exit status, stdout and stderr.
#
# Two things can never match by construction and are normalised away:
#   * the program name argparse prints, basename(argv[0]) — `test4_executable`
#     vs `test4.mjs`;
#   * the process id in the PyInstaller epilogue.
# Everything else, including full Python tracebacks, is compared byte for byte.
#
# Note: the reference resolves its recorded script path `test4.py` relative to
# the current directory, so tracebacks include the source line only when
# ./test4.py exists. The port emulates that, so run this from anywhere.
#
#   ./difftest.sh <case-file>       # one bash-quoted argv list per line
#   ./difftest.sh -                 # read cases from stdin
set -u

REF=${REF:-/workspace/dataset/test4_executable}
PORT=${PORT:-/output/test4.mjs}

work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/difftest.XXXXXX") || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
failures="$work/failures"
: >"$failures"

norm() {
  sed -E -e 's/test4_executable/PROG/g' -e 's/test4\.mjs/PROG/g' \
         -e 's/PYI-[0-9]+/PYI-N/g' "$1"
}

run_cases() {
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
    case "$line" in \#*) continue ;; esac
    eval "set -- $line"

    "$REF" "$@" >"$work/ref.out" 2>"$work/ref.err"; refrc=$?
    node "$PORT" "$@" >"$work/js.out" 2>"$work/js.err"; jsrc=$?
    norm "$work/ref.out" >"$work/ref.out.n"; norm "$work/js.out" >"$work/js.out.n"
    norm "$work/ref.err" >"$work/ref.err.n"; norm "$work/js.err" >"$work/js.err.n"

    problem=""
    [ "$refrc" != "$jsrc" ] && problem="rc"
    cmp -s "$work/ref.out.n" "$work/js.out.n" || problem="$problem stdout"
    cmp -s "$work/ref.err.n" "$work/js.err.n" || problem="$problem stderr"

    if [ -z "$problem" ]; then
      pass=$((pass+1))
    else
      fail=$((fail+1))
      {
        printf 'ARGV: %s   [mismatch:%s]\n' "$line" "$problem"
        printf '  rc     ref=%s js=%s\n' "$refrc" "$jsrc"
        printf '  stdout ref=%s\n' "$(tr '\n' '|' <"$work/ref.out.n")"
        printf '  stdout js =%s\n' "$(tr '\n' '|' <"$work/js.out.n")"
        printf '  stderr ref=%s\n' "$(tr '\n' '|' <"$work/ref.err.n")"
        printf '  stderr js =%s\n' "$(tr '\n' '|' <"$work/js.err.n")"
      } >>"$failures"
    fi
  done
}

if [ "${1:--}" = "-" ]; then run_cases; else run_cases <"$1"; fi

printf 'pass=%s fail=%s\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -gt 0 ] && cat "$failures"
exit 0

mkdir -p /tmp/w && cat > /tmp/w/gen.py <<'PYEOF'
import sys

def bq(arg: bytes) -> str:
    """bash ANSI-C quote a byte string ($'...')."""
    out = []
    for b in arg:
        c = chr(b)
        if c == "'":
            out.append("\\'")
        elif c == "\\":
            out.append("\\\\")
        elif 0x20 <= b <= 0x7e:
            out.append(c)
        else:
            out.append("\\%03o" % b)
    return "$'" + "".join(out) + "'"

def case(arg: bytes) -> str:
    return "--a " + bq(arg)

def bstr(body: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"%d:%s" % (len(body), body)

lines = []
seen = set()
def add(arg: bytes):
    l = case(arg)
    if l in seen:
        return
    seen.add(l)
    lines.append(l)

# ---- 1. single-byte top-level bodies: every argv-carryable byte 0x01..0x7f
for b in list(range(0x01, 0x20)) + [0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x27, 0x2f, 0x5c, 0x5d,
                                    0x60, 0x7b, 0x7c, 0x7d, 0x7e, 0x7f]:
    add(bstr(bytes([b])))

# ---- 2. ordered pairs from the interesting set
PAIR = [b"'", b'"', b"\\", b"\t", b"\n", b"\r", b"\x01", b"\x7f", b"a"]
for c1 in PAIR:
    for c2 in PAIR:
        add(bstr(c1 + c2))

# ---- 3. triples over the three quoting-relevant bytes
Q3 = [b"'", b'"', b"\\"]
for c1 in Q3:
    for c2 in Q3:
        for c3 in Q3:
            add(bstr(c1 + c2 + c3))

# ---- 4. realistic mixed bodies
BODIES = [
    b"it's",
    b'say "hi"',
    b"both ' and \" here",
    b"back\\slash",
    b"double\\\\slash",
    b"trailing\\",
    b"\\'",
    b"'\\",
    b"\\\"",
    b"\"\\",
    b"tab\there",
    b"nl\nhere",
    b"cr\rhere",
    b"crlf\r\nx",
    b"\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m",
    b"bell\x07",
    b"vt\x0bff\x0c",
    b"del\x7fdel",
    b"\x01\x02\x03\x1e\x1f",
    b"\\x41",
    b"\\t",
    b"\\n",
    b"\\r",
    b"\\\\x41",
    b"a'b\"c\\d\te\nf\rg\x00" .replace(b"\x00", b"\x7f"),
    b"'''",
    b'"""',
    b"'\"'\"'",
    b"\"'\"'\"",
    b"quote'in\"mix\\and\tctl\x1f",
    b" leading and trailing ",
    b"~!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>/?",
    b"0123456789",
    b"\x7f\x7f\x7f",
    b"\n",
    b"\r",
    b"\t",
    b"\n\n\n",
    b"\t\\t\t",
    b"'\n'",
    b'"\n"',
    b"\\\n",
    b"\x1f\x20\x7e\x7f",
]
for b in BODIES:
    add(bstr(b))

# ---- 5. nested in a list (single element)
NEST = [b"'", b'"', b"\\", b"\t", b"\n", b"\r", b"\x01", b"\x7f", b"it's", b'say "hi"',
        b"a'b\"c", b"\\\\", b"\x1b", b""]
for b in NEST:
    add(b"l" + bstr(b) + b"e")

# ---- 6. lists with several elements (quote choice is per-element)
add(b"l" + bstr(b"'") + bstr(b'"') + b"e")
add(b"l" + bstr(b'"') + bstr(b"'") + b"e")
add(b"l" + bstr(b"a'b") + bstr(b'a"b') + bstr(b"a'b\"c") + b"e")
add(b"l" + bstr(b"\\") + bstr(b"\t") + bstr(b"\n") + bstr(b"\r") + b"e")
add(b"l" + bstr(b"'") + b"i42e" + bstr(b'"') + b"e")
add(b"l" + b"l" + bstr(b"'") + b"e" + b"l" + bstr(b'"') + b"e" + b"e")
add(b"ll" + bstr(b"a'b") + b"ee")
add(b"l" + bstr(b"\x7f") + bstr(b"\x01") + b"e")

# ---- 7. nested in dicts
for k in [b"'", b'"', b"\\", b"\t", b"\n", b"\x01", b"\x7f", b"k'k"]:
    for v in [b"'", b'"', b"\\", b"\n", b"v\"v"]:
        add(b"d" + bstr(k) + bstr(v) + b"e")
add(b"d" + bstr(b"'") + bstr(b'"') + bstr(b'"') + bstr(b"'") + b"e")
add(b"d" + bstr(b"a'b") + b"l" + bstr(b'a"b') + b"e" + b"e")
add(b"d" + bstr(b"\t") + b"d" + bstr(b"\n") + bstr(b"\r") + b"e" + b"e")
add(b"d" + bstr(b"") + bstr(b"'\"") + b"e")
add(b"d" + bstr(b"'\"") + bstr(b"") + b"e")

# ---- 8. clamped length prefixes that truncate mid-escape-worthy byte
add(b"9:it's")           # clamp
add(b"99:a'b\"c\\d")
add(b"1:'\"")            # trailing data -> TypeError
add(b"2:'\"")
add(b"3:'\"")
add(b"0:'")              # trailing
add(b"5:\t\n\r")
add(b"100:" + b"'" * 5)
add(b"100:" + b'"' * 5)
add(b"100:" + b"\\" * 5)
add(b"l100:it's" + b"e")
add(b"l9:\te")

# ---- 9. bodies that swallow container terminators
add(b"3:aeb")
add(b"l2:ee" + b"e")
add(b"d2:'e" + bstr(b"x") + b"e")

# ---- 10. unknown leading byte = control char (prints ordinal then AssertionError)
for b in [0x01, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0d, 0x1b, 0x1f, 0x22, 0x27, 0x5c, 0x7f, 0x20]:
    add(bytes([b]))
    add(b"l" + bytes([b]) + b"e")

# ---- 11. long body with every printable + control byte argv can carry
allb = bytes([b for b in range(0x01, 0x80)])
add(bstr(allb))
add(b"l" + bstr(allb) + b"e")
add(bstr(bytes(range(0x01, 0x20))))
add(bstr(bytes(range(0x20, 0x40))))
add(bstr(bytes(range(0x40, 0x60))))
add(bstr(bytes(range(0x60, 0x80))))

sys.stdout.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
PYEOF
python3 /tmp/w/gen.py > /tmp/fuzz-repr.txt && wc -l /tmp/fuzz-repr.txt && head -20 /tmp/fuzz-repr.txt
cd /tmp && line="--a \$'3:a\\'b'" ; echo "$line"; eval "set -- --a \$'3:a\\'\"b\"'" ; printf '%s' "$2" | od -c | head -3

cd /tmp && grep -n "a'b" /tmp/fuzz-repr.txt | head -5; echo "---"; while IFS= read -r line; do eval "set -- $line"; printf '%s' "$2" | od -An -c | tr -s ' ' ; done < <(grep -n . /tmp/fuzz-repr.txt | sed -n '20,24p' | cut -d: -f2-)

cd /tmp && while IFS= read -r line; do eval "set -- $line"; printf '%s' "$2" | od -An -c | tr -s ' '; done < /tmp/fuzz-repr.txt | sed -n '36,70p'
